titles.noun: What the text says of judgment

gather.name: let justice roll on like a river

own_words.text: Far be it from You to do such a thing-to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?”
But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
before the LORD, for He is coming-He is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples in His faithfulness.
Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment,

And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne. And books were opened, and one of them was the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their deeds, as recorded in the books.
“Do not judge, or you will be judged.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come under judgment. Indeed, he has crossed over from death to life.
For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.

rows.label: Justice for the poor, the fatherless, the widow, the foreigner

eg.text: You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.
He executes justice for the fatherless and widow, and He loves the foreigner, giving him food and clothing.
Learn to do right; seek justice and correct the oppressor. Defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.”

This is what the LORD says: Administer justice and righteousness. Rescue the victim of robbery from the hand of his oppressor. Do no wrong or violence to the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow. Do not shed innocent blood in this place.

rows.label: Justice and righteousness (the Hebrew pair mishpat and tsedaqah)
rows.note: Most of these verses are Hebrew, where the Berean prints “justice” for mishpat and “righteousness” for tsedaqah or tsedeq. A few are Greek (John 16:8, Acts 24:25, 2 Cor 3:9, 2 Tim 4:8): there “righteousness” stands beside the Greek words for judgment (krisis, krima), condemnation (katakrisis) or the judge (kritēs), which are other words, and the page does not make them one with the Hebrew.

eg.text: For I have chosen him, so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just, in order that the LORD may bring upon Abraham what He has promised.”
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne; loving devotion and faithfulness go before You.
But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
But the LORD of Hosts will be exalted by His justice, and the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness.

rows.label: In the gate and the court: judges, elders, witnesses, bribes; trials and sentences

eg.text: You are to appoint judges and officials for your tribes in every town that the LORD your God is giving you. They are to judge the people with righteous judgment.
You are to go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who presides at that time. Inquire of them, and they will give you a verdict in the case.
Hate evil and love good; establish justice in the gate. Perhaps the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.”
While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.

rows.label: The king and the throne: “the king for judgment”, kings who do justice, the throne
rows.note: In Isa 9:7, 16:5, 32:1 and Jer 23:5 the king the prophet describes is one whom readers take differently; the page does not choose.

eg.text: He would get up early and stand beside the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone had a grievance to bring before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out and ask, “What city are you from?” And if he replied, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel,”
When all Israel heard of the judgment the king had given, they stood in awe of him, for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.
Of Solomon. Endow the king with Your justice, O God, and the son of the king with Your righteousness.

Of the increase of His government and peace there will be no end. He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish and sustain it with justice and righteousness from that time and forevermore. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.

rows.label: The LORD's justice and judgments: “a God of justice”, “true and just are Your judgments”

eg.text: He is the Rock, His work is perfect; all His ways are just. A God of faithfulness without injustice, righteous and upright is He.
Therefore the LORD longs to be gracious to you; therefore He rises to show you compassion, for the LORD is a just God. Blessed are all who wait for Him.
Righteous are You, O LORD, and upright are Your judgments.
And I heard the altar reply: “Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and just are Your judgments.”

rows.label: Justice asked of God, and the answer: “God has deprived me of justice”, “Does God pervert justice?”, “Where is the God of justice?”
rows.note: The complaint and the answer stand together as the text has them: Job says God has taken away his justice (27:2), Elihu that God does not pervert it (34:12), and those Malachi speaks to ask “Where is the God of justice?” (2:17). The page does not choose between them.

eg.text: “As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice-the Almighty, who has embittered my soul-
Indeed, it is true that God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.

You have wearied the LORD with your words; yet you ask, “How have we wearied Him?” By saying, “All who do evil are good in the sight of the LORD, and in them He delights,” or, “Where is the God of justice?”
Why do you say, O Jacob, and why do you assert, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God”?

rows.label: Justice turned away and perverted among people: “justice is turned away”, “in the place of judgment there is wickedness”, “the denial of justice and righteousness in the province”
rows.note: Here the verses speak of people turning justice away: the people's own words in Isa 59 (“justice is far from us”, 59:9), what Ecclesiastes saw in the place of judgment (3:16; 5:8), “to deny a man justice before the Most High” (Lam 3:35), and the wicked who hem in the righteous (Hab 1:4). They are set apart from the row before, where justice is asked of God.

eg.text: So justice is turned away, and righteousness stands at a distance. For truth has stumbled in the public square, and honesty cannot enter.
Furthermore, I saw under the sun that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.

If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official is watched by a superior, and others higher still are over them.
Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.

rows.label: Judgments on Egypt, Moab, Edom, Babylon, Sidon, Thebes; judgments on Judah, Israel and Jerusalem

eg.text: On that night I will pass through the land of Egypt and strike down every firstborn male, both man and beast, and I will execute judgment against all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
When My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens, then it will come down upon Edom, upon the people I have devoted to destruction.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I Myself am against you, Jerusalem, and I will execute judgments among you in the sight of the nations.
Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, for he is determined to follow worthless idols.

rows.label: A judge, the Judge; “all judgment to the Son”
rows.note: The text names the judge in several ways: “God, the Judge of all” (Heb 12:23), “the One appointed by God as Judge of the living and the dead” (Acts 10:42), “the righteous Judge” whom Paul calls “the Lord” (2 Tim 4:8), “one Lawgiver and Judge” (Jas 4:12), “the Judge is standing at the door” (Jas 5:9), and also earthly judges and the judge in Jesus' parable of the widow (Luke 18:2). In John 5:22 the Father “has entrusted all judgment to the Son”; in John 9:39 Jesus says “For judgment I have come into this world”. Where the verse says only “the Lord” or “the Judge”, readers take it of the Father or of Christ, and the page does not choose.

eg.text: May the LORD be our judge and decide between you and me. May He take notice and plead my case and deliver me from your hand.”
in joyful assembly, to the congregation of the firstborn, enrolled in heaven. You have come to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
And He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that He is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead.
Furthermore, the Father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the Son,

rows.label: Judgment on the nations and the world; justice for the nations
rows.note: Isa 42 and 51 speak of justice going out to the nations; Matt 12:18-20 quotes Isa 42:1-4. Who the Servant of Isa 42:1 is, readers take differently; the page does not choose.

eg.text: “Here is My Servant, whom I uphold, My Chosen One, in whom My soul delights. I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will bring justice to the nations.
Now judgment is upon this world; now the prince of this world will be cast out.
Then Jesus declared, “For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind may see and those who see may become blind.”
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I Myself am against you, Jerusalem, and I will execute judgments among you in the sight of the nations.

rows.label: The day of judgment, the hour of judgment; “at the judgment”; “after that to face judgment”; the judgment seat of God; the court seated, the books opened
rows.note: Ps 1:5 (“the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous”) is read of a court and of the last day, and the page does not choose; it also stands in “In the gate and the court”. The Hebrew “Day of the LORD” texts (Joel 1:15, Amos 5:18, Zeph 1:14, Isa 13:9) use other words and are not on this page; Isa 13:13 and Zeph 1:15 are on the wrath page, Amos 5:18 is on the light page, and the sheep and the goats (Matt 25:31-46) is gathered with this page.

eg.text: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.
Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment,

rows.label: Judgment and works, deeds
rows.note: Set side by side with the rows on condemnation and on believing, as the text has them; a verse that names more than one stands in each. Where Christian traditions part on how judgment by works stands to being counted righteous by faith, the page takes no side.

eg.text: and come out-those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.

rows.label: Condemnation, and “no condemnation”; “does not come into judgment”
rows.note: The Greek κατάκριμα and κατάκρισις, “condemnation”. Rom 5:16-18 sets the judgment that followed one trespass “to condemnation” beside the gift that follows many; Rom 8:1 says there is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus; John 5:24 says the one who hears and believes “does not come into judgment”. Set beside the row on works, as the text has them. Where Christian traditions part on how these stand to one another, and on how far “all” reaches in Rom 5:18, the page takes no side.

eg.text: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.

rows.label: Justice with loving devotion, mercy, grace: “The LORD loves righteousness and justice”; “mercy triumphs over judgment”
rows.note: The text's own pairs. The page does not say how they are reconciled.

eg.text: The LORD loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of His loving devotion.

rows.label: Judgment and what follows, in the text's own words: eternal, fire, destruction, Gehenna
rows.note: The words the verses use: “eternal judgment” (Heb 6:2), “eternal destruction” (2 Thess 1:9), “eternal fire” (Jude 7), “destruction of the ungodly” (2 Pet 3:7), “the fire of hell” (Matt 5:22) and “the sentence of hell” (Matt 23:33), where the Greek is geenna in both. Where Christian traditions part on what follows the final judgment -- punishment without end, an end of the wicked, or the restoration of all -- the page takes no side; it sets the verses as they stand. This row holds only verses that use a word for judgment: the sheep and the goats (Matt 25:31-46), gathered with this card, is not in it.

eg.text: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to his brother, ‘Raca,' will be subject to the Sanhedrin. But anyone who says, ‘You fool!' will be subject to the fire of hell.
instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.

rows.label: Judgment falling on particular acts: murder, resisting authority, eating and drinking without recognizing the body, would-be teachers, oaths, defrauding widows, turning grace into license
rows.note: Among them: murder (Matt 5:21), resisting authority (Rom 13:2), eating and drinking without recognizing the body (1 Cor 11:29), would-be teachers (Jas 3:1), oaths (Jas 5:12: “fall under judgment”), defrauding widows of their houses (Mark 12:40: “greater condemnation”), ungodly men who turn the grace of God into a license for immorality (Jude 4), the angels who sinned, “held for judgment” (2 Pet 2:4), and Rom 3:8, “their condemnation is deserved”.

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Among them: the breastpiece of judgment and the Urim (Exod 28:15-30; Num 27:21) and the lot (Prov 16:33); Jude 9, where the Greek is “a judgment of blasphemy” and the Berean prints “slanderous charge”. About 163 verses where the Hebrew mishpat means statute, ordinance or custom (for example Deut 4:5 and Lev 18:4) are another sense of the word and are not shown on this page.

rows.label: God judges, and is asked to judge: “the Judge of all the earth”, “May the LORD judge between us”, “vindicate me”

eg.text: Far be it from You to do such a thing-to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?”
before the LORD, for He is coming-He is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples in His faithfulness.

rows.label: Jesus: “I judge”, “I do not judge”, “has entrusted all judgment to the Son”, “who will judge the living and the dead”
rows.note: By hand: the verses where the text itself names Jesus, Christ or the Son, or has Jesus say “I”. They sit side by side as they stand -- “I judge no one” (John 8:15), “I do not judge him” (John 12:47), “I judge as I hear” (John 5:30), “the word I spoke will judge him on the last day” (John 12:48) -- and the page does not reconcile them.

eg.text: Furthermore, the Father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the Son,
You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.

I charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead, and in view of His appearing and His kingdom:

rows.label: Judging by one the verse calls “the Lord”, “He”, “the One” or describes: “the Man He has appointed”, “Faithful and True”
rows.note: The text says “the Lord”, “He”, “the One”, or describes him -- “Faithful and True” (Rev 19:11), “the Man He has appointed” (Acts 17:31), “Him who is ready to judge” (1 Pet 4:5), “One who seeks it and judges” (John 8:50). Readers take these of the Father or of Christ, and the page does not choose.

eg.text: My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me.

rows.label: Told to judge, and promised judging: “judge righteously”, “judge for yourselves”, “the saints will judge the world”, “twelve thrones”
rows.note: Set beside the row that follows, as the text has them; the page does not say how they are reconciled.

eg.text: You must not pervert justice; you must not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the rich; you are to judge your neighbor fairly.
Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly.”
Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if you are to judge the world, are you not competent to judge trivial cases?

rows.label: Told not to judge, and rebuked for judging: “Do not judge, or you will be judged”, “who are you to judge your neighbor?”, “stop judging by outward appearances”

eg.text: “Do not judge, or you will be judged.

rows.label: The judges: Moses, the judges of Israel, Samuel, the king, elders and priests judge the people; “who made you ruler and judge over us?”, “judged Israel twenty-three years”
rows.note: In Isa 11:3-4 the one who “will judge the poor with righteousness” is the shoot from the stump of Jesse (11:1); whom the verse means readers take differently, and the page does not choose.

rows.label: Judged, and believing, faith: “whoever believes in Him is not condemned”, “by faith Noah ... condemned the world”
rows.note: These two rows are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking. Mark 16:16 stands in the longer ending (16:9-20) that the earliest manuscripts lack. Where Christian traditions part on how faith and works stand to the judgment, the page takes no side.

eg.text: Whoever believes in Him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe has already been condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God's one and only Son.

in order that judgment may come upon all who have disbelieved the truth and delighted in wickedness.

rows.label: Judged, and works, deeds, ways: “according to each one's work”, “according to his deeds”, “according to your ways”
rows.note: These two rows are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking. Where Christian traditions part on how judgment by works stands to being counted righteous by faith, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Judging the earth, the peoples and the nations; judging the living and the dead
rows.note: Where Christian traditions part on the final judgment and what follows it -- punishment without end, an end of the wicked, or the restoration of all -- the page takes no side; the verses are set as they stand. Rev 20:12-13 and 1 Pet 4:6 are among the hardest, and are here.

rows.label: Condemn, condemned: “neither do I condemn you”, “who is the one who condemns?”, “will condemn this generation”
rows.note: The Greek verb κατακρίνω. And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God, which you possess, are to appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people west of the Euphrates-all who know the laws of your God. And you are to teach these laws to anyone who does not know them.

words.note: κριτικός is “able to discern”: “It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart” (Heb 4:12).

eg.text: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

These also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink: Priests and prophets reel from strong drink and are befuddled by wine. They stumble because of strong drink, muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments.
this would also be an iniquity to be judged, for I would have denied God on high.
Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
knowing that such a man is corrupt and sinful; he is self-condemned.
